ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every director, shareholder, beneficial owner, authorized signatory, agent, and commercial counterparty must be continuously screened against OFAC SDN, the UN Consolidated List, the financial sanctions and autonomous sanctions regimes administered by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, the list maintained by the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit, and the People's Republic of China and Hong Kong SAR designated lists when engaging in Asia-Pacific matcha distribution. Politically Exposed Persons, by status, family, or close association, require enhanced due diligence with verified source of wealth, senior management approval, and periodic review. Negative hits must be documented in a timestamped and auditable screening report, and automated real-time alerts must remain active throughout the corporate life and before each cross-border Swift TT or wire transfer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register online name availability check and Name Reservation application portal (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or te reo Māori and may use Latin-based letters with appropriate diacritics. Any name in another script must be phonetically transliterated to Roman characters, and the proposed name must not be identical or almost identical to an existing registered or reserved name under the Companies Act 1993. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) a unique leading identifier; (2) a permitted descriptive element; (3) the statutory company type suffix 'Limited' or 'Tapui Limited'; and (4) the absence of restricted expressions unless prior approval from the responsible ministry has been obtained.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection notice from the Registrar, the applicant must file a formal application for reconsideration with the New Zealand Companies Office within 15 working days, setting out why the proposed name does not give rise to confusion, false implication, or contravention of sections 21 and 22 of the Companies Act 1993. If the Registrar confirms the refusal, the applicant may apply to the District Court for review of the adverse decision, and in parallel may file a fresh name reservation with additional disambiguating words.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not inherently unlawful for registration under the Companies Act 1993 as long as the registered office is a physical street address in New Zealand capable of receiving legal process and maintaining statutory records. However, for a cross-border matcha powder wholesale entity using Swift TT and wire payment rails, leading New Zealand banks and Inland Revenue require substantive commercial substance: physical or verifiable operational premises, local invoicing, documented trade contracts, and accessible records. A pure virtual mailbox with no staff, no inventory, and no local office is treated as a shell-structure red flag and is rejected by most licensed banks for non-resident account opening and by Inland Revenue for GST or place-of-effective-management determinations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Companies Office verification that the registered office is an actual physical address; (2) Inland Revenue questionnaires or desk audits on place of central management and control; (3) bank KYC visits or video inspections of trade premises; (4) New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit AML/CFT inspection under the Act; (5) local authority or customs inspection of matcha storage and organic certifications. Quantified risk of unannounced physical inspection in the first twelve months is approximately 8% to 15% for a standard low-risk wholesale entity, but increases to above 60% if Inland Revenue issues a residence inquiry or a bank flags virtual-office-only substance and dormant transactional activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), principally sections 10 (Incorporation), 16 (Certificate of Incorporation), 37-41 (Constitution), 92-97 (Appointment of Directors), 128-131 (Board Resolutions), 124-127 (Company Records), and 270-273 (Registered Office and Delivery Address).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), administered through the Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 (Incorporation Application) submitted electronically via the New Zealand Companies Office online Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand company law does not impose a minimum paid-up share capital requirement. Shares may be issued without payment in cash or other property; however, if the board resolves to issue shares for non-cash consideration, the consideration must be lawful and fully described in a directors' resolution. No escrow or blocked account rule applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] LIMITED (the 'Company') duly convened and held on [Date], at [Time], at [Place/Conference Bridge], at which the following persons were present throughout and constituted a quorum: [Name(s) of Director(s)]. The Chairperson noted that the Company was incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 on the date set forth in the Certificate of Incorporation and that the registered office is situated at [●], New Zealand.

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board acknowledged receipt of the Application for Incorpation and recorded that the Company shall have full power to issue a maximum of [●] ordinary shares in accordance with the rules set forth in any Shareholders' Agreement or Constitution. The Board resolved that [●] fully paid ordinary shares of no par value be issued and allotted to the subscriber(s) named in the Application for Incorporation, and the Board authorised the Directors to issue share certificates or maintain electronic register entries evidencing such allotments. The Board confirmed that the aggregate consideration recorded for each allotted share has been approved and is lawful in accordance with sections 52 through 60 of the Companies Act 1993.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board resolved that the Company's principal bank account, to be established at [●] Bank, be opened and that the following persons be and hereby are appointed as authorized signatories for and on behalf of the Company, any two to sign jointly: [Director A], [Director B], and [Company Secretary]. Each signatory is empowered to execute banking documents, negotiate instruments, approve SWIFT TT and wire transfer instructions, and manage all operational financial transactions, subject to the company's internal authorization limits and anti-money laundering compliance policies.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board adopted as the registered office of the Company the address [●], New Zealand, and instructed the officers to file Form 15 and Form 16 with the New Zealand Companies Office within ten (10) working days after the date of this resolution. All corporate records, registers, and statutory books shall be kept at that address or at such other location as the Board may from time to time designate in accordance with section 127 of the Companies Act 1993.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board appointed [Name] as Managing Director, [Name] as Company Secretary, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, each effective immediately. The Board resolved that such officers shall have the power to execute all documents, to supervise the daily management of the Company, and to make all necessary filings with the Companies Office, the Inland Revenue Department, and other governmental agencies. The Board authorised the affixing of the common seal (if any), the execution of deeds, and the opening of any subsidiary operational accounts.

5. GENERAL AUTHORITY: The Board confirmed that these resolutions may be cited in any banking agreement, real estate lease, security instrument, or regulatory filing, and that this First Board Resolution shall remain in full force and effect until revoked or amended by a subsequent resolution. A certified copy of this resolution shall be supplied by the Company Secretary to any authority or counterparty upon reasonable request.

RESOLVED FURTHER that each director and officer be and is hereby authorized to execute any necessary ancillary documents. The meeting was closed. /s/ Chairperson

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Directors’ Consent via NZBN / Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz) in conjunction with the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prior to incorporation, the applicant must verify that no identical or confusingly similar company name exists in the New Zealand Companies Register. The applicant must submit a Name Reservation Application through the online portal, using the exclusive name 'ORGANIC MATCHA POWDER TRADE LIMITED' or another available name ending with 'Limited'. Concurrently, each proposed director must complete the online Director Consent Form and supply their residential address, date of birth, and evidence of identity (e.g. passport or national ID). The application must be notarized only where the director resides overseas and uses a certified copy of identity documents; otherwise, digital signing via RealMe login is sufficient. The registry will issue an NZBN automatically upon approval.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Application (Form 2)
Director Consent Forms for each director
Notarized passport copy (for non-resident directors)
Registered office address details (physical New Zealand address)
Residential address verification for directors
Digital RealMe authenticated account or authorized agent credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused because it is identical or too similar to an existing name, select up to three alternate names and file a fresh reservation within one business day. If director identity verification is queried, submit certified copies via a notary or diplomatic agent within five business days; the Registry will hold the application open for a maximum of 5 working days before cancellation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register online filing system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The authorized applicant or an agent must complete Form 1 (Application for Incorporation) by entering the reserved company name, the proposed registered office address, the mailing address, and the names and consent details of the first directors and shareholders. The application must be electronically signed by the sole (or first) director or by the authorized agent, and the prescribed government fee of approximately NZD 90 (USD 64) must be paid by credit card or internet banking. The Registrar will check the application against the Companies Act 1993 sections 14-16 and, if satisfied, issue the Certificate of Incorporation and the NZBN instantly via the online portal. The applicant must download and retain the certificate as proof of legal existence.
required_dossiers: Reserved company name (valid 20 working days)
Form 1 – Incorporation Application
Consent to act as director forms
Registered office physical address in New Zealand
Mailing address (may be outside New Zealand if director consents)
Payment of filing fee by credit card or electronic debit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or rejected, the registry will issue a notice specifying the statutory defect. The applicant may cure by amending the electronic form and resubmitting within 15 working days; if the name has expired during the suspension, re-reserve a name and pay an additional reservation fee. A formal judicial review is available via the High Court if the Registrar wrongly refuses a registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Constitution and First Board Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The Company itself, acting through its directors; external counsel for drafting; New Zealand Companies Office for any voluntary constitution filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one week of incorporation, the directors shall physically or virtually convene an inaugural board meeting in accordance with section 128 of the Companies Act 1993. The company may rely on the First Schedule (default constitution) or adopt a bespoke constitution prepared by legal counsel; if a bespoke constitution is adopted, a copy must be kept at the registered office and filed with the Registrar only if it contains special condition clauses. The Board must formally adopt the First Board Resolution covering share allotment, banking authorization, registered office address, and statutory officer appointments for the directors, secretary, and CFO. All minutes must be signed by the chairperson and entered into the share register within 10 working days.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Draft or default constitution (First Schedule)
Minutes of First Board of Directors Meeting
Share allotment schedule and share register initial page
Consent forms for statutory company officers
Written authority for banking signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office queries a missing constitution or improper officer appointment, the company may submit correcting Form 16 (Change of details) and a certified board resolution ratifying the original acts. If the board meeting is challenged, directors may obtain unanimous written shareholders' consent under section 122 to validate all resolutions retrospectively.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, GST and IRD Number Acquisition
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand, via the IRD Business Registration portal (or the incorporation link-through from the Companies Register).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after incorporation, the company must apply for an IRD number to satisfy income tax registration obligations. If taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in the next twelve months, the company must simultaneously register for Goods and Services Tax (GST); voluntary GST registration is also permitted for a trading entity anticipating frequent zero-rated exports of matcha powder. The registration can be performed online at ird.govt.nz using the NZBN. The company must decide its balance date (generally 31 March) and file an election if otherwise. A myIR business account must be opened, and the company should record the IRD number for all customs and cross-border payment purposes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Company registered office and mailing address details
Business activity description (ISIC 4631 / matcha powder wholesale distribution)
Expected annual turnover and GST registration declaration if required
Bank account details once opened
Managing director's IRD identity documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried due to activity code mismatch or missing bank details, the applicant can amend the online registration under the 'Business Information' tab and resubmit. If GST registration furtherance requires imported supplier invoices, the company may file a paper IRD form and acknowledge a slower 10-working-day processing window. Any late registration penalty may be remitted by making a voluntary disclosure and providing reasonable cause.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – the entity engages in cross-border procurement and wholesale distribution of culinary and ceremonial grade matcha powder under ISIC 4631; it performs no physical manufacturing, packaging, chemical transformation, or warehousing activities in New Zealand.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – no industrial/manufacturing operating license is required. General business trading is permitted without a specific license. Imported matcha must comply with MPI (Ministry for Primary Industries) biosecurity and food safety import standards, but this does not constitute an industrial operating permit for statutory formation purposes.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable in relation to corporate formation. If physical repacking or food handling occurs in the future, the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) and local Territorial Authority under the Resource Management Act 1991 would apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no EIA required for pure distribution and trade. Any future physical food processing or repacking would be classified as a Permitted Activity under the relevant District Plan unless significant discharges or hazardous emissions are proposed, in which case a resource consent application to the local council would trigger a 'Client' EIA tier under Schedule 4 of the RMA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable while distribution-only. For future processing sites, wastewater discharge must comply with the National Environmental Quality Standard (NEQS) and Trade Waste Bylaw limits (e.g. BOD5 < 200 mg/L, suspended solids < 250 mg/L); VOC emissions must comply with local air discharge thresholds; hazardous waste shall be handled under the Hazardous Substances and New Organisms Act 1996 with disposal manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for a non-industrial office-based trading company unless physical goods warehousing or repacking is later undertaken. Should warehousing commence, the entity must obtain a Fire Safety Certificate for fire evacuation schemes, complete structural load certification for racks, and register the building as a workplace under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 with a Worker Engagement and Participation system.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue, New Zealand (Te Tari Taake), electronic registration and filing portal myIR at ir.govt.nz; New Zealand Customs Service operates the Trade Single Window for export clearance
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity must apply for a New Zealand IRD number before carrying on a taxable activity. For an NZ-registered limited company, incorporation with the New Zealand Companies Office results in automatic allocation of an IRD number. For an offshore non-resident entity, the non-resident company must submit the Commissioner-prescribed IRD number application via myIR or approved paper procedure, providing certified incorporation documents, registered office and overseas address details, expected business activities, projected turnover, and any GST registration election. Identity verification is completed through notarised documents and, where required, appointment of a New Zealand tax or customs agent. The same IRD number is used for income tax and GST. Mandatory GST registration arises once 12-month taxable turnover exceeds NZD 60,000, although voluntary registration is available for start-up activities; the GST registration confirmation is issued electronically through myIR.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No United States-style check-the-box election exists. Available statutory elections include the look-through company election under the Income Tax Act 2007 for qualifying closely held companies, consolidated group election for wholly-owned New Zealand resident companies, and GST group registration under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Hybrid mismatch rules are enacted through the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 annual taxable turnover in any 12-month period; voluntary registration is permitted below this threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory electronic invoicing, and no anti-fraud digital stamping regime. e-Invoicing is voluntary and operates through the New Zealand Peppol Authority framework; GST returns are filed electronically through myIR, and export zero-rating claims must be substantiated by underlying transaction and customs evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods qualifies for zero-rating where the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, including goods exported within the statutory timeframe and goods supplied to a New Zealand recipient for export in the ordinary course of business. Services supplied to non-residents located outside New Zealand may also be zero-rated to the extent the services are not supplied to a person in New Zealand and the services are not substantially performed in New Zealand. The claim is recognised on the GST return and must be supported by contemporaneous evidence of physical export, foreign buyer identity, and receipt of foreign consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: NZ Customs electronic Export Declaration submitted through the Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export from New Zealand
Commercial invoice and purchase order identifying the overseas buyer and matcha powder commodity
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or New Zealand bank foreign exchange/TT advice evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Packing list and certificate of origin identifying organic matcha powder (HS heading 0902)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may reassess any improperly zero-rated supply as standard-rated at 15%, charge use-of-money interest from the original due date, and impose tax shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994, ranging from 20% for failing to take reasonable care or taking an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. Criminal prosecution and significant monetary penalties apply where export documentation is fraudulent, and zero-rating is retrospectively clawed back if goods are diverted, returned, or not exported within the statutory timeframe absent lawful Customs approval.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully liberalized and convertible currency regime under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989 and the Foreign Exchange Control Regulations (repealed). There are no capital account or current account exchange controls, no surrender requirements, and no restrictions on acquisition or disposal of foreign currency by residents or non-residents. The New Zealand dollar is classified as a free-floating currency. Corporate entities may maintain foreign currency bank accounts, convert funds freely at market rates, and repatriate dividends, royalties and loan repayments without prior approval. Capital for investment, inter-company loans and trade financing flows across the border without licensing, although large cross-border transfers may trigger reportable thresholds only for statistical purposes by the Reserve Bank. Profit remittance by a non-resident-owned entity is subject only to standard corporate governance approvals and possible non-resident withholding tax on dividends; no administrative exchange control approval is required. Banking settlement occurs via the Exchange Settlement Account System and SWIFT corridors, with same-day NZD clearing through the Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system. Therefore the principal practical risk for a matcha distribution treasury is not convertibility denial but strict anti-money laundering documentation and bank counterparty due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender provisions exist in New Zealand. Under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Foreign Exchange Transactions) Exemption Notice, exporters may retain 100% of foreign currency export proceeds indefinitely, convert at will, or use them for overseas settlement without mandatory conversion timeline. There are no ratios.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: NZD Capital Escrow Account and Foreign Currency Operational Account
NZD Escrow and Trade Settlement Account
NZD Transaction Account with SWIFT all-in-one token

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: New Zealand does not legally bar foreign payments fintechs from servicing corporates if they are registered under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 as a financial institution or money changer; however, such EMIs are typically not licensed banks and do not offer local NZD Bank Settlement Account clearing codes, documentary letters of credit, or statutory capital verification vouchers. Viability is therefore Medium for ancillary receivables/payables but Low as a substitute for a tier-1 domestic bank in escrow or trade settlement. Engage only if the EMI maintains an agency arrangement with a New Zealand registered bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 NZ banks under the AML/CFT Act generally require the statutory director(s) to undergo a physical identity interview at an authorised branch for non-resident directors, unless the bank accepts verified identification through a recognized New Zealand notary public or consular officer and completes a video conference with the compliance officer. Remote consular proxy opening is permissible for routine current accounts but fully discretionary for trust and corporate structures; tailored onboarding with a relationship manager typically mandates one in-person visit to Auckland for signatories and director before wire limits are lifted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained high-risk reference on sanctioned or politically exposed person watches lists of a shareholder or beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn source of funds letter, valid passport notarized by gazetted official, negative sanctions screening report from World-Check or Dow Jones, Certificate of Good Standing from NZ Companies Office, tax residency certificate, six months of personal bank statements, and if PEP, a transaction audit trail to establish legitimacy of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between registered business scope (matcha powder distribution) and expected banking turnover of millions in early stage with no commercial history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved business plan, executed purchase contracts from Japan/China suppliers, end-customer purchase orders, warehouse lease evidence, insurance policies covering goods in transit, freight forwarding bills of lading, prior year audited financial statements if available, and capital injection proof with source.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Operation of a holding structure involving a foreign trust or subsidiary where beneficial ownership chain has multiple layers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate organizational chart, trust deed or registered deed, register of members with certified identities of settlor/protector/beneficiaries, certificate of incorporation of each intermediate entity, Council of the Institute of Chartered Accountants certification of beneficial ownership analysis (or equivalent independent audit), and a legal opinion from an NZ-licensed solicitor stating the structure is not designed for evasion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming rapid net-worth or third party payments to the operational account without corresponding trade documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transaction narrative, intercompany agreements, commercial invoices, shipping documents, import/export entry documents from New Zealand Customs, bank confirmation of correspondent institution, and monthly reconciliation reports.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route injections via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'Cross-border inter-company financing' or 'Trade settlement' in the free-format narrative; utilize a New Zealand registered bank receiving account with entity legal name exactly matching Companies Office record. For equity injections, issue share allotment resolution and file capital contribution with Companies Office (company register). For loan injections, execute written loan agreement and maintain register of charges to avoid disguised interest issues. Obtain a capital verification certificate from the external auditor or chartered accountant if the bank's compliance committee requires. No Reserve Bank approval is required, but any transfer exceeding NZ $50,000 must have complete source-of-funds evidence available to the bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SWIFT MT103 for low-value/high-frequency supplier payments; Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) at sight for large matcha purchase contracts, especially Japanese or Chinese exporters requiring documentary security; Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) for balanced risk. Settlements clear via the correspondent network and NZ RTGS for NZD legs; foreign currency disbursements are executed via nostro accounts. Use Incoterms and customs declarations to harmonize with banking documents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Short-term outward FX forwards up to 12 months to lock USD/JPY/NZD matcha procurement costs
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the NZD for counterparties without a NZD clearing line
Cross-currency swaps limited to balance-sheet hedging of intercompany loans' principal and interest, not speculative

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 1993, s 216) — annual confirmation of company details, directors, shareholders, and share structure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment, MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within the company's annual 'return month', being the calendar month of the incorporation anniversary; filing must be completed by the last day of that month (e.g., incorporated 15 May → due 31 May each year). The Registrar issues a reminder at least 28 days before the due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the return remains unfiled, the Registrar issues a compliance/default notice; an annual return more than 28 days overdue, or a second consecutive missed return, triggers a Notice of Intention to Remove under s 319 of the Companies Act 1993, leading to administrative strike-off and dissolution of the company. Directors may additionally be prosecuted; on summary conviction the fine is up to NZD 10,000 (≈ USD 6,100).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial Statements and Auditor's Report (mandatory filing only if the company is 'large' or an FMC reporting entity; otherwise financial statements must still be prepared for directors and Inland Revenue)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE) — electronic filing; copy to shareholders in accordance with Companies Act 1993, ss 200–210
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the balance date. For a standard 31 March balance date, financial statements (where required) must be completed and filed by 30 September; a shareholder copy must be provided at least 20 working days before any annual meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare, audit, or file is an offence under the Companies Act 1993 and the Financial Reporting Act 2013; each director is liable on conviction to a fine of up to NZD 10,000 (≈ USD 6,100). The Registrar may also apply for removal of a persistently defaulting company from the register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: IR4 Company Income Tax Return (annual ancillary tax filing supporting corporate good standing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Standard 31 March tax year: due 7 July following year-end for companies not represented by a tax agent; non-standard balance dates: due by the 28th day of the sixth month after balance date. An IRD-approved tax agent extension may defer the filing date to the following 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250 (≈ USD 150) on day one, plus NZD 50 (≈ USD 30) for each full month the return remains outstanding (capped at NZD 500 ≈ USD 300); use-of-money interest on unpaid terminal tax at the IRD prescribed rate (≈ 9–11% per annum), with additional late payment penalties if tax remains unpaid after demand.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Return of Allotment and Notification of Director / Registered Office Changes (event-driven statutory filings during the year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Return of Allotment: within 10 working days after each share allotment. Director appointment or cessation: within 20 working days. Change of registered office: notification filed with the Registrar before the change is effective against third parties.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing is an offence; directors are liable to fines of up to NZD 10,000 (≈ USD 6,100) on conviction. Failure to notify creates defects in the public register, may render an allotment/registration ineffective, and exposes directors to civil liability for loss caused to the company or third parties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A small NZ private trading company is generally audit-exempt. A mandatory independent audit applies under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and Companies Act 1993 only if the company is 'large' for two consecutive accounting periods (total assets exceeding NZD 60 million OR turnover exceeding NZD 30 million), or if it is an FMC reporting entity (publicly accountable), or if shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting shares requisition an audit, or if the company's constitution requires an audit. An NZ limited company engaged in matcha powder distribution will normally fall below these thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For-profit entities must report under NZ IFRS (New Zealand equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards); entities without public accountability may adopt the Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR) pursuant to XRB A1. Small companies not required to report under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 may prepare special-purpose financial statements for directors and Inland Revenue, but the accounting records and GST/tax reconciliations must still satisfy IRD record-keeping standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a separate annual UBO declaration for private companies. Beneficial ownership is confirmed annually through the Annual Return, which must list each shareholder's full legal name, address, and shareholding as at the return date, together with current director details. All share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the next Annual Return; new share allotments must be filed with the Companies Office within 10 working days, and director changes within 20 working days. For AML/CFT purposes, banks and financial institutions identify and verify beneficial owners at account opening and on an ongoing risk-based basis; this is a financial-sector due diligence obligation, not a corporate registry filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (recording share transfers, allotments, and trustee/beneficial holding notes where applicable)
Register of Directors (full names, residential addresses, dates of appointment and cessation)
Minute Books of Directors' and Shareholders' Meetings (including written resolutions)
Accounting Records (retained for 7 years; kept at the registered office or another Registrar-approved location)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $200 – $600 per annum (registered office address, registered agent, and company secretarial maintenance by a New Zealand corporate services provider or chartered accountant)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,000 – $8,000 per engagement (typical fee of a CA ANZ-accredited audit firm for a small-to-medium trading company; not incurred while the statutory audit exemption applies)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (resident company final income tax rate under the Income Tax Act 2007, s BC 18 and s LF 1)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential sectoral rates in New Zealand; the effective rate may be reduced by normal deductible expenses, depreciation, approved research and development tax credit of 15%, and imputation credits when profits are distributed; a wholesale matcha distribution company will generally be taxed at the 28% headline rate on New Zealand assessable income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_statutory_rule: Unlimited / indefinite carry-forward under Subpart IA of the Income Tax Act 2007, subject to the 49% shareholder continuity test and, if continuity is breached, the same-business test. There is no statutory five-year time limit for New Zealand resident companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Return of Income for a Company, filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR secure online portal; paper filing is no longer the standard compliance route for a New Zealand registered company.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due on 7 July of the same calendar year if the taxpayer is not represented by a tax agent; where an approved tax agent extension applies, the filing date is normally 31 March of the following year. For non-31 March balance dates, the return is due by the 7th day of the fourth month after balance date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, IRD number, registered office address, and tax balance date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name as filed with the New Zealand Companies Office; if the company is ultimately controlled from outside New Zealand, still use the New Zealand registered legal entity and New Zealand IRD number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity / ANZSIC industry classification, e.g., cross-border wholesale of organic matcha powder.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use an accurate description of the matcha wholesale, procurement, and distribution activity; the New Zealand company's tax residence status is not altered by the description of overseas sourcing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income / assessable income derived during the income year, including New Zealand and foreign source income of the New Zealand resident company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A New Zealand incorporated limited company is tax resident in New Zealand and must declare worldwide income subject to applicable foreign-source exemptions and active-business exclusions under the CFC rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenditure / expenses directly attributable to earning assessable income, including cost of matcha powder, shipping, insurance, warehousing, staff costs, and professional fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only amounts supported by contemporaneous records; document cross-border related-party supply costs under the arm's length standard. Payments to Hong Kong-related counterparties require transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carry-forward utilised in the current year, subject to shareholder continuity requirements and any business continuity election.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the shareholding in the NZ Ltd has changed, verify that 49% continuity is satisfied before utilising losses; otherwise the loss may be quarantined.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after deduction of carried-forward losses and any net exempt or excluded income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute taxable income using New Zealand source rules and tax treaties; retain a full arm's length reconciliation for every related-party sale of matcha powder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable at the company tax rate, less imputation credits attached to prior dividend receipts, less foreign tax credits, and less any provisional tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not complete this field; the New Zealand company computes tax at 28% and must record NRWT to be withheld on any dividend distribution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties are imposed under s 139AA of the Tax Administration Act 1994; an initial late filing penalty of NZD 250 applies, with further penalties accruing on continued non-filing. Unpaid income tax attracts use-of-money interest under s 120C, and shortfall penalties under s 141 may be imposed, ranging from 10% to 150% of the potential revenue loss. In extreme cases, the company and directors may face criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on dividends is 30% at the statutory rate; a fully imputed dividend is subject to NRWT at 15% under domestic law. Double tax agreements may reduce the rate to 15% for portfolio dividends and in many cases to 5% for direct holdings of at least 10% of voting power, provided the beneficial owner satisfies treaty and residence requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced NRWT rate under a double tax agreement (DTA) between New Zealand and Hong Kong, the beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department and deliver it to the New Zealand paying company before the dividend is paid. The New Zealand company must retain the TRC, an attestation of beneficial ownership, and any supporting organisational chart or corporate records demonstrating eligibility. If the full 30% NRWT is withheld because the documentation is not available in time, the non-resident may apply to Inland Revenue for a refund of the excess withholding; such claims are accepted only where treaty entitlement is proven and the applicable limitation-on-benefits and beneficial ownership tests are satisfied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory NRWT rate on cross-border royalties and interest from New Zealand is 30%. Under most New Zealand DTAs, royalty withholding is reduced to 10% and interest withholding to 10% or 15%, subject to the beneficial ownership rule and any anti-treaty-shopping provision. Qualifying interest payments may instead attract the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% where the investor is unrelated to the borrower and the security satisfies the public-issue test; an arm's length interest rate is still required under the transfer pricing rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Local File is mandatory where a New Zealand company or group has aggregate cross-border controlled transactions exceeding NZD 5 million in an income year. A Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required where the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds NZD 1.2 billion (approximately EUR 750 million). For smaller groups, contemporaneous records that reasonably support the arm's length result remain good practice and may be requested by Inland Revenue.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as found in certain offshore financial centres; however, the Income Tax Act 2007 contains robust general anti-avoidance rules (Subparts GB and GA), and the common law doctrines of sham and economic substance remain fully applicable. A New Zealand matcha distribution company must demonstrate genuine local management and control, maintain physical or verifiable business substance (e.g., an office or qualified staff, procurement contracts, board minutes and operational records), and ensure that profit attribution to New Zealand is not artificially displaced. Failure to meet these standards may cause Inland Revenue to disregard the entity's separate identity, to reattribute income, to deny treaty and NRWT benefits, or to impose shortfall penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a false IR4 return, understating organic matcha turnover, fabricating supplier invoices, claiming personal or non-deductible expenses, or destroying business records to avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under s 143 of the Tax Administration Act 1994; imprisonment of up to 5 years for a natural person; fines of up to NZD 50,000 for an individual and NZD 100,000 for the company; shortfall penalties may increase the total liability by up to 150% of the tax avoided.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign, direct, or knowingly assist in filing false returns face individual prosecution, personal criminal fines, and imprisonment. Inland Revenue may issue a Departure Prohibition Order barring the director from leaving New Zealand while tax is unpaid, and the director may be disqualified under the Companies Act 1993.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling matcha powder to a related Hong Kong distributor at a deliberately depressed margin, paying excessive royalties or management fees to a related offshore service provider, or failing to prepare contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for cross-border related-party transactions exceeding NZD 5 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may make an arm's length price adjustment under s GC 8 of the Income Tax Act 2007, denying deductions or increasing assessable income; a shortfall penalty of 20% to 40% applies for an abusive tax position, and a penalty of up to 150% applies where the avoidance is evasive or fraudulent; late payment interest is also charged from the original due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute non-arm's length pricing can be treated as personally involved in tax avoidance; civil liability may extend to an equalisation of profit, a reinstatement of withheld tax obligations, and personal fines. Withdrawal of travel documents via a Departure Prohibition Order is a practical remedy available to Inland Revenue while a director remains personally liable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recharacterising dividend distributions from the New Zealand company to its Hong Kong shareholder as interest, service fees, product royalties, or repayments of shareholder loans in order to reduce or eliminate non-resident withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may apply the anti-avoidance provisions and reclassify the payment as a dividend subject to NRWT at 30% or the applicable treaty rate; unpaid NRWT is recoverable as a debt to the Crown, and a shortfall penalty of 20% to 150% may be imposed. Failure to withhold and remit NRWT is a serious criminal offence where done knowingly.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who cause or permit a distribution to be paid without the required NRWT deduction may be personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax, together with interest and penalties. A director could also be subject to a Departure Prohibition Order until the debt is settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham Shell Company / No New Zealand Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the New Zealand company purely as a booking centre with no office, no employees, no substantive decision-making, and no business records, while the real trading decisions for the organic matcha powder supply chain are made in Hong Kong.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The arrangement may be void for tax purposes under s GB 1 or the common law sham doctrine; profits will be reattributed to the real controller, treaty benefits may be denied, NRWT at 30% may be imposed on hidden distributions, and penalties for false declarations may be assessed. In some circumstances the company may be treated as a resident of Hong Kong under the tie-breaker test, losing New Zealand tax residence benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign declarations of New Zealand residency or substance when none exists are exposed to criminal liability for false statements, disqualification, and personal liability for taxes, penalties, and interest arising from the reattribution of income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: DTA / Treaty Abuse Through Hong Kong Conduit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Hong Kong intermediate company with negligible employees or activity solely to access the New Zealand–Hong Kong double tax agreement and reduce the dividend withholding tax rate on distributions flowing to a beneficial owner who is not resident in Hong Kong.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue will deny treaty relief if the Hong Kong company is not the beneficial owner or lacks sufficient substance; the full 30% NRWT is then payable, together with interest and a shortfall penalty of up to 150% under the abusive tax position provisions. The transaction may also be challenged under the principal purpose test embedded in New Zealand's tax treaties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the New Zealand payer who knowingly process dividends through a conduit without verifying treaty entitlement may be personally liable for the unpaid NRWT, interest, and penalties; a departure prohibition order may additionally prevent them from leaving New Zealand.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using false or inflated invoices for matcha powder purchases to justify cross-border wire transfers from New Zealand to Hong Kong, or structuring payments to conceal the true beneficial owner or the true nature of the underlying trade.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Actions of this type are prosecutable as tax evasion and as money laundering under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and the Proceeds of Crime Act 1991. A reporting entity may be fined up to NZD 10 million for serious corporate non-compliance; fraudulent invoices can also trigger civil forfeiture and confiscation of the proceeds of crime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors or compliance officers who participate in or knowingly permit such activity face criminal prosecution, imprisonment of up to 7 years, personal fines, disqualification, and liability to confiscation orders; they may also be prohibited from leaving New Zealand pending the resolution of the tax and forfeiture matters.
